identity_notes: Ginkgo is by far the most extensively studied identity in this partition (79 kept human records of 152 screened, after excluding a large number of records about Ginkgo-Damole/Ginkgo Diterpene Lactone Meglumine IV injection products, unrelated broad reviews, and animal/in-vitro studies). Evidence for the flagship indication (dementia/cognitive decline prevention) is genuinely mixed and dose/population-dependent: the large NIH-funded GEM RCT (19017911/20040554, n=3069, NCT00010803) found NO reduction in dementia incidence or cognitive decline in normal/MCI older adults; the most current Cochrane review (41641880, 2026, 82 studies/10,613 participants) finds only small-to-moderate benefit specifically in people with DIAGNOSED dementia (not MCI or subjective cognitive complaints), with most evidence low-to-moderate certainty and possible increased adverse-event risk in the subjective-complaints subgroup. Several EGb761-specific meta-analyses at the 240 mg/day dose (25114079, 26819725, 39895346) do find statistically significant cognitive/ADL benefits specifically in dementia populations. Healthy-population cognitive enhancement (memory/attention/executive function) shows consistently null results (23001963 meta-analysis; 12186600 large single RCT). For tinnitus, the most current Cochrane review (36383762, 2022) found little-to-no effect with very-low-certainty evidence. For intermittent claudication, the Cochrane review (23744597) found no clinically significant benefit and flagged likely publication-bias inflation of even the modest pooled effect. Safety: ginkgo LEAF extract has a well-documented bleeding-risk signal via antiplatelet potentiation, especially combined with anticoagulants/antiplatelets/NSAIDs (handoff items above); separately, raw ginkgo SEEDS (not leaf extract) carry a distinct, serious ginkgotoxin poisoning risk, especially in children -- a materially different exposure from standardized leaf-extract supplements that should not be conflated with it. Many Chinese trials use Ginkgo only as an ADJUVANT/add-on to conventional treatment (stroke, intracerebral hemorrhage, delirium) or in FIXED COMBINATION with another active drug (cilostazol, ticlopidine, prednisone, Ginkgo-Damole) -- these cannot be used as evidence for standalone ginkgo extract supplementation and are flagged related_form_differs/different_material throughout. One retracted publication (36199780) was excluded from any efficacy conclusion.
